free_tier.stated: "Small projects may request up to 8'000 node hours on Alps. Such projects may not exceed the granted allocation and are limited to a one-year duration." A Preparatory Project is the entry step and "is allocated a total of 250 node hours over 3 months on the HPC vCluster on Alps". Small proposals are assessed by technical evaluation only, with acceptance "within two months from submission", and no fixed deadline.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The quarterly reset is what makes this record useful beyond a simple rejection: a 8,000 node-hour annual allocation arrives in three-month windows and expires unused, so a workload that needs a continuous month of GPU time does not fit the shape even inside the institution.

limits.value: "Small projects are intended for applicants from the Swiss user community" and every proposer "must hold at least a postdoctoral position at an academic institution", so the 8,000 Alps node-hours need a Swiss academic appointment before any technical review begins.
